title: Account Review Accelerator: Standard + Enterprise QBR Slate
body:
Purpose:
This is a working kit for QBR decks that scales from a light, 6-slide Standard account review up to a fuller Enterprise slate (10–14 slides) with renewal runway and risk mitigation playbooks baked in. Use as a starting point for Customer Success Managers to run consistent, efficient reviews that tie product telemetry to business outcomes and renewal asks.

Audience:
- CSMs preparing QBRs for mid-market and enterprise customers
- Customer Success leadership reviewing deck quality and coverage
- Solutions/SEs joining for technical slides or milestone sign-offs

How to use this file:
1) Pick the template (Standard or Enterprise) that matches account tier and time since last touch.
2) Fill the data snapshots from the Renewal Runway sheet and from Redwood Console: token spend, latency SLOs, error rates, model mix.
3) Add customer-specific narratives in the "Storyline" fields below. Keep slides focused on 1–2 insights each.
4) Mark any open asks with the "Action + Owner" pattern to avoid ambiguity.

Standard (6-slide) — Lean narrative for adoption-focused accounts - Slide 1: Title + objective. Speaker note: 1 sentence objective for this QBR (e.g., "Align on adoption plan and secure renewal conversation in 90 days").
- Slide 2: Topline health snapshot (Usage, Cost delta, NPS/CSAT)
  Data to show: 30/90/365 day tokens, avg latency, #automations live.
- Slide 3: What changed / wins since last QBR (3 bullet timeline)
  Speaker note: cite 1 customer quote and 1 measurable improvement from Console metrics.
- Slide 4: Opportunities to accelerate value (3 prioritized plays)
  Format: Play name | Expected impact | Effort estimate | Who helps (SE/Eng)
- Slide 5: Renewal runway & next steps (Goal, Risks, Ask)
  Show: renewal date, target tier, required ramp.
- Slide 6: Appendix / Action tracker (owner + due date)

Enterprise (10–14 slide) — Deep-dive for strategic customers
- Slide 1: Executive one-liner & meeting objectives
- Slide 2: Customer success brief (top metrics, adoption map, exec sponsor list)
- Slide 3: Product telemetry & performance (Redwood Console charts: latency P50/P95, model mix by % tokens, error breakdown)
- Slide 4: Business outcomes tied to product usage (e.g., conversion lift, support deflection)
- Slide 5: Adoption heatmap (feature-by-team usage matrix)
- Slide 6: Risk & mitigation quadrant (Impact vs Likelihood) — populate with a short remediation plan per risk
- Slide 7: Cost & efficiency review (current run rate, optimization opportunities like batching/quantization, estimated $ savings)
- Slide 8: Roadmap alignment & integration asks (what Redwood will deliver vs customer-owned items)
- Slide 9: Renewal economics and options (list 3 commercial levers: committed capacity, reserved pool, custom SLA)
- Slide 10: Proof-lane: short case study or internal pilot metrics
- Slide 11: Decision calendar & recommendation (dates, approvals needed)
- Slide 12: Action tracker + owners + escalation ladder
- Slide 13–14: Appendices (data pulls, queries, technical deep-dive notes)

Renewal Runway Tracker (sample columns — paste into shared sheet):
- Renewal date
- Current ARR (USD)
- Current monthly token run-rate
- Forecast at renewal (tokens & $)
- Adoption score (0–100)
- Engagement health (meetings/month)
- Risk flag (green/amber/red)
- Primary risk owner (CSM/SE/PM)
- Mitigation step 1 (owner + due)
- Comms cadence (weekly/bi-weekly)

Suggested Queries / Data pulls (copy/paste examples)
- Token spend by model, last 90 days: SELECT model, SUM(tokens) FROM usage WHERE customer_id = '<<ID>>' AND ts > dateadd(day, -90, current_date) GROUP BY model;
- Latency distribution: export P50/P95 from Console request metrics for the last 30 days.
- Feature usage by team: join events table to team IDs, aggregate active users per feature.

Speaker-Notes Patterns (short scripts)
- "Topline: Over the last 90 days we saw X% increase in tokens, driven by ModelA trials in two product flows. Our P95 latency improved from 1.8s to 1.1s after we rolled out prefix caching. The next step to reach your target of Y is…"
- "Risk: If ModelA usage grows 3x we expect cost delta of ~$Z/month. Proposed mitigation: enable quantized variant + batching during non-peak windows; SE to own pilot."

Action Tracker Template (copy to slide appendix)
- ID | Action | Owner | Due | Status | Related ticket (jira)
- Example: CS-1 | Kickoff model optimization trial | Samir Patel (SE) | 2025-03-10 | In progress | JIRA-CS-10567

Meeting Facilitation Cheat-Sheet
- 0–5min: Open + objective (set expectations)
- 5–20min: Topline health (keep this tight for execs)
- 20–40min: Deep-dive (product telemetry or business outcome)
- 40–50min: Ask + decision (be explicit about the decision needed)
- 50–60min: Actions and close (read back owners and confirm next meeting)

Open questions / TODOs (internal)
- Which Redwood Console charts are authorized to be shared in customer decks? (legal check)
- Decide on standard naming for "adoption score" — propose scaled mix of DAU, token growth, and feature breadth.
- Track a/b performance of "cost optimization" play to measure lift (CS-10234).

Notes to CSMs (short reminders)
- Never bury the ask — state the renewal/expansion ask on slide 1 and again during the decision section.
- Use the risk quadrant to make mitigation tangible and owned.
- Attach the renewal-runway sheet link in calendar invite.

Appendix: Quick examples of impact language
- "By shifting 30% of traffic to a lower-precision variant we project a 22% reduction in token spend with <3% quality delta on your core prompts."
- "A short pilot with Dedicated capacity for model X would reduce 95th latency by ~400ms for heavy batch inference windows."

Versioning and review flow
- v0.1 (this doc): internal draft for CSM team feedback
- v0.2: incorporate SE inputs and sample data
- v1.0: centralized template for all Standard accounts

Contact / owner
- Document owner: Avery Chen (CS Enablement) — reach via Slack #cs-deck-kit or avery.chen@redwood.ai

End of kit.
